folkways.ponder.book_modes.header: One book, three things a click can mean
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_1: A left click with the book acts on the world. Which of three things it does shows on the book itself.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_2: Pointing: a left click takes the block or the body under your crosshair into the colony, or back out of it.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_3: Sneak and scroll turns the book to the next gesture. A second book keeps whatever it was left in.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_4: Marking out: that same click draws a box instead, one click on each of two opposite corners.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_5: Hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) and scroll. Before the box is framed this sets a reach, and a Ctrl click drops a corner that far out, in open air. Once it is framed, it pushes the face you aim at in or out.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_6: Then right click. The panel asks what the ground is for, and the answers come from the parts of Folkways you have installed: a farm, a pasture, a building, and so on.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_7: Drawing a line: each left click adds a stop, joined to the one before, up to 4096 of them. A right click asks what the path is for.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_8: Sneak and left click throws the box or line you are drawing away.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_9: Aimed at a zone or path already marked out, right click opens its settings, whichever gesture the book is in. Anywhere else, it opens the colony panel.
folkways.ponder.building.header: Building: draw it, and the colony raises it
folkways.ponder.building.text_1: With the book marking out, frame the ground and pick Pattern from what the box can become. A line drawn with the book offers it too.
folkways.ponder.building.text_2: Then choose a pattern and its few settings, down to the blocks it is made of. Folkways ships a few, data packs add more under folkways/pattern, and your own go in the folkways/pattern folder of your game.
folkways.ponder.building.text_3: Residents with the building trade take the order. First they clear what stands where the drawing wants empty space, working down from the top.
folkways.ponder.building.text_4: Then they lay it from the bottom up, a cell at a time, with blocks fetched from the colony's stores.
folkways.ponder.building.text_5: While you hold the book, the blocks still to go show as ghosts, and a card over the site counts the cells laid and lists, under Still needs, what the rest will take.
folkways.ponder.building.text_6: A cell with nowhere in reach to stand gets a column of scaffolding beside it, taken from the stores. Once that part is laid it comes down, and the scaffolding goes back.
folkways.ponder.building.text_7: The Building page lists every build order with its cells done out of the total. Deleting one stops the work and takes any scaffolding it put up back down.
folkways.ponder.building.text_8: A pattern such as the mine grows in rounds: once one round is built, the next is drawn onto what stands now. The page says which round is coming up.
folkways.ponder.building.text_9: In creative mode, a drawing you confirm stands up at once.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.header: A colony is the blocks you mark
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_1: A colony book is crafted from a plain book. It is how you reach your colonies, not what makes them yours.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_2: A right click opens the colony panel. Before you keep any colony it offers one button, New Colony. Press it, and you are the new colony's founder.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_3: The colony goes with you, not the book: any colony book opens it. Click the title of the panel to switch between your colonies, or to found another.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_4: Left click a chest with the book and it joins the colony as storage. Click it again to take it back out.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_5: Besides containers, only blocks some part of Folkways puts to use can join: a work station, a bed. What each is for is shown where it is used.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_6: Anything else is refused: the colony has no use for it.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_7: Bodies take the same click. Pointed at one of your own residents, it lets them go.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_8: A colony is not a patch of ground you fence off. It is the blocks you marked yourself.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_1: A right click with the book opens the colony panel. Its pages are listed down the left side, in three groups.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_2: Under Colony come its own pages. Workforce sets each resident's work priorities, and Storage lists what the colony's containers hold.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_3: Storage lists every item held in the colony's containers, with how many. Refresh counts again.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_4: At the foot of Settings, Delete colony ends the colony for good. It only goes through once you type out the phrase it asks for.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_5: Under Production, every installed part of Folkways adds a page: Workshop for the stations, Household for the beds, and so on. Their own lists live there, like the fuel stations may burn and the food residents may eat.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_6: Under Preferences, Settings holds the colony's Tools list. Residents only take up tools on it, and an empty list allows none. It starts out with every tool some work asks for.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_7: Lessons holds a folder for every installed part of Folkways. Open one to watch a single lesson, or all of them in a row.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_8: Anywhere in the panel, hover a page's tab and hold the ponder key to play the lesson for that page.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.header: Handing a Create schematic to the colony
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_1: With Create installed, a schematic you have put in place with Create's own tools can go to the colony instead of to a schematicannon.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_2: Hold the schematic, and the colony's book in your other hand.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_3: The schematic's tools have one more among them: Hand Off, marked with the colony book. Choose it and right click.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_4: A small window asks one thing: what to do with cells the blueprint leaves empty. Leave what stands there, which it starts on, or dig it out.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_5: Place the build order. It is filed where the schematic stands, turned and mirrored the way you set it.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_6: From there it is a build order like any other: residents raise it, and it shows on the Building page. It is never raised at once, not even in creative.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.header: Dispatch: order from a Create package network
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_1: A package network built with Create: stock behind a packager and a stock link, and a Stock Ticker to order from. The colony orders from it only by what it ships on: every packager hands its parcels to frogports beside it, all on one chain net, turning and in one dimension; or to a postbox beside it, set to a station. Should that stop being so, the colony orders nothing until it is put right, though residents still take from its containers by hand. Let nothing else take from those packagers, or orders go astray.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_2: With the book pointing, left click the stock link or the Stock Ticker: the colony takes the network on. Left-click a frogport or a chain conveyor: the colony takes that whole chain net on. Left-click a postbox: the colony takes that postbox on, and sends by it only aboard trains it has taken on. The same click gives each back. The network orders only once what it ships on is the colony's too.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_3: A network locked in Create can only be handed over by someone allowed to run it.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_4: A Stock Ticker is a desk. A resident with the Dispatch trade sits on a seat beside it, on the same level or one below, and keeps it.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_5: The colony only orders from a network with its own keeper at the desk. With nobody there, the stock is counted but out of reach.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_6: Every Package Frogport on a chain net the colony holds is a pick-up point, except the ones beside the network's packagers, where parcels set out, and the ones over a container, which empty what they catch into it. So is every postbox the colony holds that one of its trains runs to. The colony sends to whichever point is handiest. A point whose address is exactly * or contains any of { } , \ is never used by the colony on its own.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_7: When the colony needs goods the network has in stock, it sends for them to a pick-up point. A hauler waits for the parcels and takes out what was ordered.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_8: Parcels nobody here is waiting for are emptied as well, so strays do not fill the pick-up point.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_9: The Dispatch page lists the networks taken on, whether someone is at the desk, each pick-up point, and what is on the way.
folkways.ponder.farming.header: Farming: draw a plot, and let it come back
folkways.ponder.farming.text_1: With the book marking out, click two opposite corners to frame a plot. Its settings say what it grows, wheat here, and whether residents pull up grass and flowers before hoeing; both are on to start.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_2: Residents hoe the ground inside the box. A hoe is the one tool a plot asks for, and the Tools list under Settings has to allow it: an empty list allows none.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_3: Then they sow it, and come back when the crop is ripe. Crops that don't need farmland, like cane or saplings, are sown without hoeing.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_4: Most crops leave the soil bare once harvested, and the next round is sown on the same ground.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_5: Sugar cane is cut once it stands three tall, bamboo at four, and only down to the bottom stalk. What stays keeps growing on its own. Bamboo is sown two rows at a time with an aisle left between, so nobody is walled in.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_6: Melons and pumpkins give up the fruit only. The vine is left standing and grows another one. Vines are sown a cell in from the edge of the plot, and the fruit grows in the ring left round them.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_7: A wood lot is a plot whose crop is a sapling. The same cycle: every log of the tree is felled with the leaves it holds up, all of it carried off, and a sapling goes back where one has room to grow. Dark oak goes in four to a square, and jungle and spruce can too.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_8: A farmer with the Replant perk resows as they harvest, using a seed from what the crop just dropped. It only works for crops cut down whole, like wheat, not for cane, fruit or trees.
folkways.ponder.fishing.header: Fishing: frame the bank, not the water
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_1: A fishery frames the bank the residents stand on.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_2: Never the water itself. Frame the bank, and the water within reach of it is what gets fished.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_3: Each fishery fishes the one block of water nearest its bank, and two fisheries never share one. If that block is already taken, the second fishery sits idle.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_4: A rod is the one tool a cast asks for, and it has to be on the Tools list under Settings.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_5: Then they stand there and wait out the bite. The line running to the float is how you tell fishing apart from idling.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_6: Practice shortens the wait: the Skilled Angler perk brings the bite on sooner.
folkways.ponder.groundwork.header: Groundwork: mark a box, and the ground in it is worked
folkways.ponder.groundwork.text_1: A groundwork zone does whichever work is ticked in its settings, one or several: clear, fill, weed, fell and haul. Cleared and filled together, the box is dug out and laid with the fill block; the fill block already there stays.
folkways.ponder.groundwork.text_2: Clear takes out every block in the box, from the top down, and only in the box: mark it as deep as you mean to dig. Builders do it, with the tool each block wants, and leave the colony's own blocks alone.
folkways.ponder.groundwork.text_3: Fill lays the block chosen in its settings into every open cell, from the bottom up, brought from the colony's stores.
folkways.ponder.groundwork.text_4: Weed pulls the grass and ferns in the box. Flowers are pulled only with Pull flowers ticked, and a fill never buries one. Farmers do it.
folkways.ponder.groundwork.text_5: Fell takes down every tree whose trunk stands in the box, its leaves with it. A log with no leaves of its own, in a wall or a beam, is left standing.
folkways.ponder.groundwork.text_6: Haul has the haulers pick up whatever lies loose in the box and carry it off to the colony's stores.
folkways.ponder.golems.header: Golems: put your Modular Golems to work
folkways.ponder.golems.text_1: With the book on pointing, left click a Modular Golem you own. It joins the colony as a resident; click it again and it leaves.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_2: Only the golem's owner can hand it over, and one that already belongs to another colony stays there.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_3: In the colony it drops its own goals and picks no fights, and golem command items do nothing to it. When it leaves, it gets its own ways back.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_4: It works in the trades its body allows: a metal golem hauls and builds, a dog golem only hauls, and a humanoid golem can also craft, drive and dispatch.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_5: It never eats or sleeps. Its knacks are built in, so it does not get better with practice.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_6: Below 60 percent of its health, a golem carrying something golems are repaired with, such as iron ingots, spends one from its pack to mend itself.
folkways.ponder.housing.header: Housing: a room worth coming home to
folkways.ponder.housing.text_1: Enclose the beds under a roof, with a door residents can walk through. Every open floor cell needs light of at least 8. Without these, or with fewer than four floor blocks per bed, it is only a basic bed.
folkways.ponder.housing.text_2: A suitable dormitory has at least four floor blocks per bed. For comfortable housing, allow six per bed, no more than four beds, and at least two furnishing kinds.
folkways.ponder.housing.text_3: An excellent bedroom allows up to two beds, with nine floor blocks per bed and at least three furnishing kinds. Storage, carpet, decoration and tables are the four kinds; extra copies of one kind do not count again.
folkways.ponder.housing.text_4: Keep production blocks out of an excellent bedroom. A crafting table or furnace bars the top grade even when there is enough space and furniture. Hold the book to read each bed's grade and advice.
folkways.ponder.housing.text_5: The glyph after a resident's name shows his mood: sad below 40, neutral from 40 to 69, happy from 70. With the book held, happy or angry sparks show when a reason turns into a bonus or penalty.
folkways.ponder.housing.text_6: Mood changes work speed gradually: ×0.75 at mood 0, normal speed at 60, and ×1.15 at 100. Better housing helps, along with food, rest, company and recreation.
folkways.ponder.dining.header: Dining: set a table for the colony
folkways.ponder.dining.text_1: With the book marking out, frame a dining area around tables and adjacent chairs. Top slabs make tables and bottom stairs make chairs. Include the chairs in the area and leave a clear aisle beside them.
folkways.ponder.dining.text_2: Connected table tops on the same level form one table. Residents can serve it from any reachable edge and eat from any free chair beside it; they do not need to reach each dish separately.
folkways.ponder.dining.text_3: Choose food and 1 to 4 servings per table cell in the area settings. Furniture with an inventory uses that many slots, up to its capacity. A plain top holds one placed dish, such as cake.
folkways.ponder.dining.text_4: Residents bring the chosen food from colony supplies or arrange its production, then set the table. Hungry neighbours take a free place and eat. Keep ingredients and a route to the table available.
folkways.ponder.dining.text_5: The drink list is separate from food. With compatible bar furniture installed, dining areas stock supported drink counters automatically. Diners fetch a drink with their meal; ordinary storage cabinets can instead be stocked by delivery orders.
folkways.ponder.recreation.text_1: In quiet moments residents stroll around nearby. Where flowers grow they stop and relax a while, which restores more leisure than a plain walk.
folkways.ponder.recreation.text_2: Chatting with a neighbour and spending time with pets restore leisure too. Residents choose these activities themselves, and may take a short break when leisure runs very low.
folkways.ponder.recreation.text_3: Pets may visit once at least three residents have beds in rooms graded suitable dormitory or better. Every half-day brings a chance, with mob spawning enabled and a safe place nearby; a visit is not guaranteed.
folkways.ponder.recreation.text_4: The colony can attract one pet per three well-housed residents: cats at three, wolves join the pool at six, parrots at ten. They arrive untamed. Residents also enjoy healthy pets tamed by colony members.
folkways.ponder.elevator.header: Elevators: walk in, ride and walk out
folkways.ponder.elevator.text_1: Build and power a Create elevator: a glued cabin under an elevator pulley, a moving redstone contact and matching elevator contacts at the floors. Keep the shaft clear and provide walkable landings beside the cabin.
folkways.ponder.elevator.text_2: With the book pointing, left click the elevator pulley to take it into the colony. Residents can then plan routes between its floors, even while the cabin is elsewhere.
folkways.ponder.elevator.text_3: A resident walks to the landing and waits for the cabin. When it arrives, he walks into a free standing place. Capacity comes from the clear connected deck, with room left for passing; adding seats does not add capacity.
folkways.ponder.elevator.text_4: The elevator carries standing residents to their requested floors. At the stop they walk out onto the landing and continue to work or bed. Keep the entrances and exits clear.
folkways.ponder.elevator.text_5: A full cabin leaves the next resident waiting for a later trip. A stopped or overstressed drive cannot provide a ride; keep the pulley powered and its floor contacts reachable.
folkways.ponder.tavern.header: Tavern: from the vineyard to a glass of wine
folkways.ponder.tavern.text_1: Mark a rectangular grape plot and choose grapevines. Supply trellises and grapevine plants: residents build four corner posts, each four blocks high, then a pergola over the plot five blocks above the soil.
folkways.ponder.tavern.text_2: Residents plant the vines at the feet of the finished posts. The vines grow over the pergola and hang grapes underneath; residents pick the ripe grapes. Leave room around the plot to work.
folkways.ponder.tavern.text_3: Register a pressing tub and a Tavern barrel as kitchen stations, allow the crafting trade and order wine. Residents press eight grapes into a juice bucket. Supply buckets and empty wine bottles as well.
folkways.ponder.tavern.text_4: The barrel takes four juice buckets through its top. Build a route onto it, such as a stepladder. Keep a closed tap on its side and solid ground beneath the bottle spot; after fermentation residents set out, fill and collect the bottles one at a time.
folkways.ponder.tavern.text_5: Bar cabinets hold the bottles themselves and can be stocked through delivery orders when registered as storage. Bar counters in a dining area are stocked automatically from its drink list. Choose wine there and keep the counter reachable.
folkways.ponder.tavern.text_6: After a table meal, a diner can fetch a bottle from the counter. A chair beside the counter also lets a resident sit for a drink. Drinking gives the wine's own effects and leaves the empty bottle behind.
folkways.ponder.household.text_1: Join beds to the colony with the book. Residents automatically claim a free bed; the Human residents page lists those still unclaimed.
folkways.ponder.household.text_2: Walking tires him, and so does standing at work. Tired enough, he goes back to his own bed and sleeps it off. Without a bed of his own he cannot sleep, and his housing mood is poor.
folkways.ponder.household.text_3: Work and walking consume food; time spent working and distance walked build fatigue.
folkways.ponder.household.text_4: The colony keeps food for three days in each resident's pack, and he eats when hungry. On the Human residents page, choose allowed foods or exclusions and whether food safety filters apply.
folkways.ponder.household.text_5: With no allowed food in colony stores, his pack stays empty. A starving resident loses health.
folkways.ponder.household.text_6: Hold the book, and the card over each resident nearby shows a drumstick for how full he is and a moon for how rested.
folkways.ponder.household.text_7: Hold the book to see a card over each colony bed: who sleeps there, its room grade, and advice for improving it.
folkways.ponder.orders.header: Orders: name what you want kept, the colony works out the rest
folkways.ponder.orders.text_1: An order keeps one item stocked in one container. Use the colony book on one of the colony's chests, and the Orders page that opens files the draft into that chest.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_2: The draft is an item, a Refill below mark and a Fill to count.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_3: Maintain files it as a standing order: once the chest drops below the refill mark, it is filled back up to the Fill to count. Deliver fills it to that count once, and the order is done.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_4: You order the finished goods. Fetching the grain and working it at a crafting table, stonecutter or smithing table of the colony's is the colony's business.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_5: What must be smelted goes through a furnace, blast furnace or smoker of the colony's, kept fed from the fuel list on the Workshop page: coal and charcoal, to start with.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_6: Nobody goes out to dig for an order. If the stores hold neither the goods nor what they are made from, it waits.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_7: To withdraw an order, use the colony book on its chest and press Del beside it on the Orders page.
folkways.ponder.pasture.header: Pastures: keep breeders and harvest grown surplus
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_1: Frame a pen the way you frame a plot. Choose its animal (cows, sheep, pigs or chickens), how many adults to retain from 0 to 64, and whether to shear.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_2: The Pastures page lists every pen: its animal, total head, retained adult target and current grown head. Young animals are included in the total.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_3: Below or at the target, residents feed ready adults in pairs. At the target, breeding continues for one surplus calf; feeding then waits while the surplus grows.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_4: Only grown head above the retained adult target are culled. With a target of four, six grown cows provide two carcasses; a calf never costs the herd a retained adult. A target of 0 clears every grown animal.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_5: Milk is drawn only when something in the colony asked for milk, and each cow gives it once a day.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_6: While the shear switch is on, sheep are shorn once their wool is back, and the shears must be on the Tools list under Settings. In a chicken pen, eggs are picked up where they fall.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_7: A gap in the fence shows on the pasture's card in red. A beast that walks off the ground you framed stops being counted, and the pen breeds back up to the target.
folkways.ponder.rail.header: Rail: give the colony a train to run
folkways.ponder.rail.text_1: Build and assemble a train with Create as usual. The colony can run it for you.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_2: With the colony book in your off hand, use a Train Schedule on the driver's seat of a train that has none. The train takes the schedule, and the colony takes the train on.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_3: An empty hand on the same seat, book still in the off hand, takes the schedule out and gives the train back.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_4: While the train stands at a station with its driver's seat empty, a resident with the Drive trade walks over and sits in it.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_5: Add Driver Seated to the stop's wait conditions, and the train waits there until every driver sent for has sat down.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_6: With a driver aboard, a train that calls at two or more stations and has a free seat is a way to get about. Residents on their way somewhere ride it from one of its stations to another.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_7: Add All Residents Alighted to a stop, and the train holds there until everyone getting off at that station is off.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_8: The Rail page lists each train taken on, its stations, whether it is running or at a stop, and when it has no driver.
folkways.ponder.residents.header: Residents: who comes, what they take on, how they look
folkways.ponder.residents.text_1: A newcomer needs room: a free bed joined with the book, and stored food for every resident plus one more mouth.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_2: Someone must also be waiting. Newcomers gather over time, more slowly as the colony grows, and only a few wait at once. Let one in on the Human residents page brings the next, unless the server has switched arrivals off.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_3: On the Workforce tab each resident has a cell per trade: click it to allow or forbid that trade, scroll it to rank it 1 to 4. You rank trades, never tasks, and a forbidden trade is never handed to him.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_4: Working a trade earns experience. Each level draws a trade perk; levels 3, 6 and 10 also draw a shared perk, such as a brisker walk or a bigger pack. Open the resident's window to read his trades, levels and perks.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_5: A newcomer's name and look are drawn from this colony's name pool and look pool. Either pool can be edited entry by entry, or replaced whole by a set a data pack offers. After that, a resident's own window changes his name, surname and look one by one.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_6: Struck by a mob or a player, or caught by fire, a resident drops what he is at and runs away from it.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_7: If a resident dies, everyone who keeps the colony is told.
folkways.ponder.workshop.header: The workshop: stations the colony works
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_1: Point the book at a crafting table, a stonecutter or a smithing table and it joins the colony as a station. A furnace, blast furnace or smoker joins the same way.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_2: A station needs a spot within reach and in sight of it for a resident to stand on. One walled in on every side is left out.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_3: Residents with the crafting trade work them. They make what the colony's orders call for, and fetch the ingredients from its stores first.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_4: The stonecutter works its own recipes. The smithing table is used for upgrades only, never for trims.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_5: At a furnace they put in a load and come back for it once it is cooked. A large batch is shared out among the idle furnaces of the same kind.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_6: A loaded furnace that has gone cold gets fuel one piece at a time, and only what is on the fuel list: coal and charcoal to begin with.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_7: Anything left finished in a furnace that nobody is waiting on gets taken out too, so the next load has room.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_8: The Workshop page counts the stations and lists each one, a furnace with the fuel in it or No fuel. The fuel list is the first row there.

folkways.supply.help: Creative players configure this source. Residents fetch only what their tasks need.
folkways.supply.empty: Mark a creative supply box with the colony book.
folkways.refusal.supply.source_changed: The supply box changed; plan a fresh withdrawal.

folkways.refusal.supply.out_of_reach: The resident must reach the supply box.
folkways.ponder.creative_supplies.header: Creative supplies: only what the task needs
folkways.ponder.creative_supplies.text_1: Place and configure a creative supply box in Creative mode. Choose all items, or a whitelist of items, tags and searches.
folkways.ponder.creative_supplies.text_2: Mark the box with the colony book. It supplies tasks; mark an ordinary chest separately to store their finished goods.
folkways.ponder.creative_supplies.text_3: Residents walk to the box and take only the finite amount their current job needs. A full pack or an unreachable box waits.
folkways.ponder.creative_supplies.text_4: For a full production-chain test, whitelist base ingredients only and order the final dish. Intermediate foods and finished dishes must be made by the residents.
folkways.ponder.cookery_orders.header: A colony kitchen: order the final dish
folkways.ponder.cookery_orders.text_1: Mark the kitchen stations, a crafting table and storage with the colony book. Keep a reachable place to stand beside each appliance.
folkways.ponder.cookery_orders.text_2: Give residents the crafting trade, then set a delivery or maintain-stock order for the finished dish. The colony arranges the ingredients and intermediate steps.
folkways.ponder.cookery_orders.text_3: Keep base ingredients, containers and reusable kitchen tools in accessible stores. A missing ingredient or blocked appliance leaves the task waiting without spending its inputs.
folkways.ponder.cookery_orders.text_4: The Kitchen page shows each registered appliance and its current state. Use its lessons to learn heat, shared tools, milling, cooking and farming.
folkways.ponder.cookery_heat.header: Kitchen heat: light, shelter and relight
folkways.ponder.cookery_heat.text_1: Mark the stove as a kitchen station. The colony tends its ignition separately from the food cooking above it.
folkways.ponder.cookery_heat.text_2: Lighting spends one flint-and-steel durability, or one fire charge. A native stove keeps burning without a coal slot or repeated fuel deliveries.
folkways.ponder.cookery_heat.text_3: Cooking follows the appliance's native heat rules: lit heat sources, or blocks in its heat-source tag such as magma, can supply heat.
folkways.ponder.cookery_heat.text_4: Rain or water can put the stove out. Residents wait for a dry, reachable stove instead of wasting ignition items repeatedly.
folkways.ponder.cookery_heat.text_5: Keep the interaction side and a standing place clear. Once the shelter is dry, the colony can relight the stove and cooking can continue.
folkways.ponder.cookery_millstone.header: The millstone: drive it, release it, walk clear
folkways.ponder.cookery_millstone.text_1: The nine millstone parts belong to one kitchen station. A flour order can fetch wheat and arrange a real grinding task.
folkways.ponder.cookery_millstone.text_2: Leave a reachable exit and room for the resident to circle the mill. The task checks its way out before loading any ingredients.
folkways.ponder.cookery_millstone.text_3: Passing residents are not captured. Only the assigned resident may bind as the motor; the native mill then turns and processes the actual input.
folkways.ponder.cookery_millstone.text_4: Finished grinding releases the motor immediately. The task still waits until the resident really walks clear; unbinding in place is not a completed exit.
folkways.ponder.cookery_millstone.text_5: Only then are the real output slots emptied into colony logistics. The same flour is never also left as a loose duplicate.
folkways.ponder.cookery_millstone.text_6: Cancellation and reload release the resident safely and preserve accepted ingredients for recovery. A blocked exit waits for a path; ordinary animal-driven mills keep their native behavior.
folkways.refusal.farm.no_sickle: The resident needs a shared sickle for this harvest.
folkways.settings.restore_grass: Restore short grass with bone meal
folkways.refusal.seed.no_straw_hat: The farmer needs a straw hat in the head slot.
folkways.refusal.seed.no_grass: The short grass or required bone meal is no longer available.
folkways.refusal.seed.unsafe_growth_area: Grass growth needs a clear, flat 15 by 15 grass area inside the marked zone.
folkways.refusal.seed.area_changed: The seed grassland has changed or is no longer enrolled.
folkways.page.cookery.seeds.need_hat: Needs a farmer wearing a straw hat
folkways.page.cookery.seeds.need_growth_: Needs clear, flat 15 by 15 grassland for growth
folkways.page.cookery.seeds.need_grass: Needs short grass; automatic growth is off
folkways.page.cookery.seeds.gathering: Gathering real seeds from short grass
folkways.page.cookery.seeds.need_bonemea: Needs bone meal to restore short grass
folkways.page.cookery.seeds.restoring: Restoring short grass with bone meal
folkways.page.cookery.seeds.unknown_inve: Waiting for unloaded stores or residents; composting is paused
folkways.ponder.cookery_tools.header: Shared kitchen tools: borrow for a task and return them
folkways.ponder.cookery_tray.header: The bamboo tray: exposure, real drips and reversible batches
folkways.ponder.cookery_seeds.text_6: With Restore grass enabled, real bone meal can replenish a safe, flat 15 by 15 grass patch over non-grass soil. The full native growth footprint must belong to this area. Missing bone meal, a small patch or unsafe bounds makes restoration wait.
folkways.ponder.cookery_equipment.text_5: Knives, spatulas and sickles are shared colony tools. One missing tool may be made from raw materials; a tool already borrowed makes other work wait. Return it to an available rack or warehouse after the task. Maintain orders can provide more.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tools.text_7: The colony's Tools list still controls which tools may be used. An empty allowed list permits none; more residents alone never raises the shared stock target.
folkways.ponder.cookery_spit.text_4: After native cooking finishes, the booked resident uses a real kitchen knife to collect its own batch safely. This grip protects only that task; it does not grant general fire immunity or switch off external power.
folkways.ponder.cookery_teapot.text_4: After brewing finishes, the real filled pot is picked up. The resident places one of its own cups, pours one portion from the pot's actual stored result, and takes the real filled cup. Player cup positions are never overwritten.
folkways.ponder.cookery_spit.header: The shawarma spit: real power, separate halves and a safe grip
folkways.ponder.cookery_steamer.text_3: The reachable top lid closes using the native lid rule. Lower blocks are covered by the stack above them; a half block below another steamer cannot pass its heat upward.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tray.text_2: Drying needs the native clear exposure and dry weather. An opaque roof pauses progress; an open column or suitable clear glass allows the same real batch to continue.
folkways.ponder.cookery_steamer.text_5: Collection waits until every owned portion is actually steamed. The native take-out moves all food in that block, so the task never mixes its ingredients with a player's slots.
folkways.ponder.cookery_teapot.text_3: The actual ingredient then enters the pot. Its native grace period and brewing timer both require real heat. Removing heat pauses the same accepted batch, and reload does not charge another bag or bucket.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tray.text_5: Only the actual owned result is taken. Cancellation and reload preserve accepted materials; changed player contents are refused without refunding or duplicating them. Dried leaves can then feed real tea-bag crafting and brewing.
folkways.ponder.cookery_teapot.text_2: Native filling transfers a real bucket of the recipe's fluid and returns its empty container. Water teas and milk tea use their actual different fluids; the pot is not filled by changing a display value.
folkways.ponder.cookery_rice.header: Rice: from a flooded plot to a bowl
folkways.ponder.cookery_chain.text_1: Order the final dish, such as udon noodles, and register every station along its route. The colony plans the needed intermediate foods instead of asking you to order each one by hand.
folkways.ponder.cookery_teapot.header: Brewing tea: a real bucket, a tea bag and twelve cups
folkways.ponder.cookery_rice.text_6: Order the finished rice meal. Residents connect the paddy, millstone and heated stockpot themselves. Supply the recipe's bowls and lid; missing carriers wait instead of spending the next batch.
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.text_4: Stir-fry must be collected within its native 40-second window. It then burns, and after another 20 seconds becomes real charcoal. A long interruption can lose the requested dish: spent ingredients are not refunded and the original food is not recreated.
folkways.ponder.cookery_chain.text_4: A borrowed kitchen knife cuts that dough on the actual chopping board. The native recipe gives three raw noodles; the knife returns for another task, and the real surplus noodles remain available for later orders.
folkways.ponder.cookery_equipment.text_3: A farm normally uses Pick: tea regrows from age three, tomato and chili from age five. Open that plot's Harvest mode setting and choose Sickle for native whole-harvest loot and young regrowth.
folkways.ponder.cookery_teapot.text_5: This repeats for all twelve actual portions. A failed serving transaction restores the finished pot and returns only its unspent cups; it never leaves extra filled cups while also refunding their containers.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tools.text_1: Mark a kitchenware rack as a store. Its two real slots hold one supported tool each; ordinary stores remain available when the rack is full.
folkways.ponder.cookery_steamer.text_4: A real heat source is still required. When it disappears, an owned batch cools down through the native ticker and waits for heat to return.
folkways.ponder.cookery_spit.text_5: The actual cooked portions enter colony logistics once. Cancellation and reload recover accepted food without spending the same raw ingredients again.
folkways.ponder.cookery_steamer.text_6: The real portions are delivered once, and a lid changed by this task returns to its original state. Empty or changed batches are refused instead of accidentally dismantling a steamer layer.
folkways.ponder.cookery_rice.text_3: A mature plant is one harvest. Only its bottom part yields panicles and wild seeds; the two upper parts are claimed with it, so they never pay the harvest again.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tools.text_4: The returned tool goes to an allowed rack first, then an ordinary store, keeping its name, enchantments and native wear. Only after the old tool breaks or becomes unavailable, with no usable shared tool or delivery on the way, is one replacement requested.
folkways.ponder.cookery_chain.text_6: The final order completes with the actual served dish. No station is skipped, and missing ingredients, a borrowed tool or an unfinished native timer keep the dependent step waiting.
folkways.ponder.cookery_chain.text_3: The normal crafting recipe combines flour and a water bucket into raw dough. That intermediate is real inventory, and the empty bucket returns through the same ordinary crafting logistics.
folkways.ponder.cookery_rice.text_5: Mark a reachable millstone as a kitchen station. A rice order can send a resident to drive the real mill: one panicle supplies three grains, and the resident walks safely out when finished.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tray.text_4: Wetting uses actual rain or a water-fed stalactite. Many conversions are reversible, so a later weather change may process the material again until the requested product is collected.
folkways.ponder.cookery_seeds.text_3: The Composting settings page controls automatic composting, a default seed reserve (64), and individual values for seeds the colony owns or grows. Sowing, goods in transit, task claims and explicit orders remain protected. Wild rice and rice share one reserve entry, with wild seeds kept first.
folkways.ponder.cookery_equipment.text_1: A hat in the pack has no seed effect. A grass-seed gathering task borrows one allowed straw hat, equips it and returns it afterward. Ordinary farming and kitchen work do not request a hat.
folkways.ponder.cookery_steamer.text_2: The task reserves an entirely empty block and places several real ingredients in one native interaction. Food in other blocks stays with its original owner.
folkways.ponder.cookery_equipment.text_4: The sickle is borrowed for this task. Residents cut the claimed root without sweeping a neighbor's land. Mature crops, the blacklist, sweep-enchantment wear and the ten-tick cooldown still apply; rice is counted once.
folkways.ponder.cookery_equipment.text_6: Only four genuinely equipped farmer pieces activate Cookery's water movement effect. Water tasks borrow the complete set together and return it afterward; the hat alone only enables seed loot.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tools.text_2: Idle crafting residents do not each fetch a knife. A task borrows the knife, shovel or sickle it actually needs, and keeps that same physical tool until its work is over.
folkways.ponder.cookery_chain.text_5: The stockpot route also needs its real soup base, lettuce, egg, lid and bowl. Fixed and flexible recipes may require different quantities, so a shorter ingredient list still follows native matching and quality rules.
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.text_1: Register each pot or stockpot as a kitchen station and keep its heat source lit. Leave the handle side of a stir-fry pot clear: the resident works immediately beside its handle. Players' existing ingredients and dishes are left alone.
folkways.ponder.cookery_spit.text_1: Mark either half to register one kitchen station. Each half holds its own native batch of up to eight matching campfire ingredients.
folkways.ponder.cookery_seeds.text_2: Drops use the original loot chances. Keep a rare first seed for expansion: sow it, grow it and collect its real offspring. Other seeds need their own farms or valid conversion recipes; short grass cannot supply every crop.
folkways.ponder.cookery_spit.text_3: The real redstone signal drives the native cooking clock. Removing power pauses the same batch; it does not turn raw food into a finished meal.
folkways.ponder.cookery_rice.text_2: One physical wild rice seed plants all three parts. Residents prefer wild seeds; edible rice can plant the same crop when it is the available fallback.
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.text_2: A stir-fry batch checks all its food, one oil and any serving vessels before loading. It then uses the real pot to add oil and ingredients; containers returned by those ingredients rejoin storage.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tools.text_3: One knife means one active borrower. Another task waits while it is busy or being carried; waiting never creates a second knife.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tray.text_3: The tray advances on its own native timer. The task waits for the actual completion flag instead of inventing dried leaves or skipping the recipe duration.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tray.text_1: Register a bamboo tray and order its real drying or wetting product. A task reserves one empty slot; food placed by a player in the other slots stays in place.
folkways.ponder.cookery_seeds.text_5: Level seven still matures for the original twenty ticks. At level eight a resident collects one real bone meal and empties the composter. Turning automatic composting off stops new input while mature bone meal can still be collected.
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.text_5: A stockpot batch checks its actual soup base, food, lid and vessels together. The resident fills the base, adds ingredients and closes the real lid; the native cooking timer then advances while heat and lid are present.
folkways.ponder.cookery_seeds.text_1: Register a Seed grass area with the colony book. A farmer wearing a real straw hat gathers its short grass only while obtainable grass seeds are missing. A hat does not create seeds without a real source.
folkways.ponder.cookery_chain.header: A meal order: flour, dough, noodles and the finished dish
folkways.ponder.cookery_rice.text_1: Mark a flooded dirt plot with the colony book and supply a hoe. Residents till its soil before sowing; suitable existing farmland also works. Keep water in the bottom crop space and two clear spaces above.
folkways.ponder.cookery_teapot.text_6: The one real, now-empty pot returns to its original station. The twelve filled cups and the empty fluid bucket enter logistics once; neither a duplicate pot nor twelve leftover empty cups are created.
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.text_6: Open the stockpot and serve each actual portion with its required vessel. Three rice portions spend three bowls, not six. The same real lid can serve later batches, and the next batch begins only after the previous one is fully collected.
folkways.ponder.cookery_teapot.text_1: Mark a teapot and order the finished tea. Each native recipe brews twelve portions, so the plan also supplies twelve real empty cups and leaves an accessible place to serve them.
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.text_7: Fixed recipes and flexible recipes use the native matching rules. Flexible dishes keep the quality calculated by the actual appliance. Accepted batches survive cancellation and reload; recovery takes the owned result rather than spending the ingredients again.
folkways.ponder.cookery_tools.text_6: For two parallel tasks, set a knife maintain order with both its minimum and target at two. Actual borrowed knives promised back to that store still count, so borrowing them does not manufacture spare copies.
folkways.ponder.cookery_seeds.text_4: Mark a composter. Composting needs no straw hat. Each complete batch checks the surplus again and spends the average native input count to fill level seven at once: 21 wheat seeds for an empty composter. A smaller surplus waits.
folkways.ponder.cookery_rice.text_4: Ordinary harvesting leaves water for the next planting. Replanting spends a real harvested seed. Wild seeds and edible rice share one planting reserve, with wild seeds kept first.
folkways.ponder.cookery_chain.text_2: Wheat becomes flour in the real millstone. Keep the turning path and a clear exit open: the resident must finish driving the mill and walk free before another step can use the output.
folkways.ponder.cookery_steamer.header: The steamer: layers, a top lid and real heat
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.header: Pots and stockpots: real ingredients, heat and serving vessels
folkways.ponder.cookery_tools.text_5: Only when the colony truly has no suitable tool and no real supply already underway does it ask for one replacement. Tool crafting happens before the food task, so the first crafting resident can make the first knife.
folkways.ponder.cookery_equipment.text_2: Clothing has its own allowlist. Relevant water-farming tasks may borrow a complete farmer set and return it afterward. An unrelated equipped item is never replaced. Disabling the task or clothing returns the borrowed pieces.
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.text_3: The resident borrows a real kitchen shovel and performs the recipe's native stirs. Cooking runs on the block's own timer. A dish with serving vessels needs its complete vessel count; other products are taken with the shovel.
folkways.ponder.cookery_steamer.text_1: A continuous column is one kitchen station. A half block holds four portions, a full block holds eight; heat passes upward only through full blocks, to at most four block levels.
folkways.ponder.cookery_chain.text_7: Other chains obey their own native conditions too: drying needs the right exposure, steaming needs heat and a closed lid, and tea needs real brewing and serving. Provide the stations, safe paths and base materials; the colony carries each real intermediate between them.
folkways.ponder.cookery_spit.text_2: An order uses an empty half and preserves food already placed by a player. The colony tracks only the ingredients it actually accepted.
folkways.ponder.cookery_seeds.header: Keep seeds, compost surplus, restore grass
folkways.page.cookery.pot_burnt: Burnt food; collect before it turns to charcoal
folkways.page.cookery.weather: Waiting for suitable drying or wetting conditions
folkways.ponder.cookery_pots.text_8: Normal orders use matching native recipes. Only an explicit Suspicious Stir-Fry or Dark Cuisine order chooses unmatched ingredients. Suspicious Stir-Fry is served after cooking; only a Dark Cuisine order waits for the real burnt state. An accidentally burnt normal dish does not complete its original order.
folkways.ponder.cookery_teapot.text_7: Normal tea orders use matching native recipes. Only an explicit Mystery Tea order brews an unmatched ingredient: 200 ticks of input waiting, then 2,400 ticks of native brewing with heat. It yields four real cups instead of twelve, so prepare four empty cups.

folkways.perk.global_tireless.desc: Work and walking fatigue reduced by 10%% / 20%% / 30%%
folkways.perk.hauling_heavy.desc: Carrying capacity +25%% / 50%% / 100%%; deliveries use the expanded pack
folkways.perk.hauling_batch.desc: Gather up to 2 / 3 / 4 loads sharing a source or destination; estimated extra walking is limited to 8 blocks and cargo must fit
folkways.perk.hauling_endurance.desc: Walking fatigue while hauling reduced by 15%% / 30%% / 45%%
folkways.perk.global_easygoing.desc: Negative food, housing and weather moods reduced by 15%% / 30%% / 45%%
folkways.perk.global_sociable.desc: Chatting restores 15%% / 30%% / 50%% more recreation for both participants; the stronger conversationalist applies
folkways.perk.building_prospecting.desc: Mining ordinary stone has an 4/7/11%% chance to find a mineral weighted by the local biome, height and ore generation settings. Rank III has a 15%% chance of a second find.
folkways.perk.building_fortune.desc: Blocks broken with a tool drop as if it had Fortune I/II/III; a tool with higher Fortune keeps its own. Prospecting finds are unaffected.
folkways.perk.building_quarrying.desc: Consecutive mining of the same ordinary stone builds up to +15/30/50%% excavation speed after 8 blocks. A 10-second pause resets momentum.
folkways.perk.building_tool_expert.desc: Building and excavation tool durability consumption -15/30/45%%.
folkways.perk.farming_chain_harvest.desc: Harvest 1 / 2 / 4 additional adjacent mature crops in the field, respecting reserved jobs.
folkways.perk.farming_bountiful.desc: Primary crop yield +10%% / 20%% / 35%%. Separate seed drops are unchanged.
folkways.perk.farming_care.desc: Planted and replanted crops grow 10%% / 20%% / 35%% faster. One treatment per crop.
folkways.perk.herding_fleece.desc: Shearing yields 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 extra wool of the original color on average.
folkways.perk.herding_breeder.desc: Resident-assisted breeding has a 5%% / 10%% / 20%% chance of twins, within the pasture target.
folkways.perk.herding_nurture.desc: Feeding a juvenile additionally reduces remaining growth time by 10%% / 20%% / 30%%, once per animal.
folkways.perk.fishing_school.desc: Fish catches have a 15%% / 25%% / 40%% chance of 1 / 1 / 2 extra fish of the same species.
folkways.perk.fishing_treasure.desc: Successful catches have a 2%% / 4%% / 6%% chance of an extra local discovery, controlled by loot tables.
folkways.perk.fishing_water_sense.desc: Progressively favors uncommon fish from the active local fishing loot table.
folkways.perk.crafting_batch.desc: Complete 2/3/4 runs of one recipe per operation, consuming all materials.
folkways.perk.crafting_frugal.desc: Eligible recipes refund each ingredient unit with an 5%%/10%%/15%% chance; packing recipes excluded.
folkways.perk.crafting_byproducts.desc: Eligible recipes have a 10%%/20%%/30%% chance to yield their configured byproduct.
folkways.perk.crafting_furnace.desc: Input batches personally loaded smelt 10%%/20%%/30%% faster.
folkways.perk.patrolling_martial.desc: Deal 10%%/20%%/35%% more damage to hostile creatures.
folkways.perk.patrolling_stalwart.desc: Take 5%%/10%%/20%% less damage from hostile creatures.
folkways.perk.patrolling_alert.desc: Detect threats 2/4/6 blocks farther away and share targets with nearby patrollers.
folkways.perk.patrolling_reassuring.desc: Wards grant residents +2/4/6 safety mood and make attack distress fade 20%%/40%%/60%% faster.
folkways.dining.furniture: Place adjacent tables and chairs inside the area, with an aisle beside each chair.
folkways.dining.help: Adjacent tabletops form one table. Residents can serve from any edge and share its food across seats. Basic tabletops support placeable foods; native tables replenish the configured servings per block. Native bar counters inside the area store two bottles each and are stocked automatically. Place a chair beside a counter with an aisle next to it so residents can sit and drink in their spare time.
folkways.dining.no_food: The selected food does not suit these tables. Kaleidoscope Cookery tables display edible items; basic tabletops need supported placeable foods, such as cake.
